study_type_evidence.quote: Two month old wild-type C57BL/6 mice (Charles River) were intravenously injected with 50 μL of 40 μM cyclized CTX:Cy5.5 through the tail vein.
Serum stability assays were carried out in 100% human male serum (Sigma) using a peptide concentration of 20 μM.

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: two month old wild-type C57BL/6 (Charles River) for the serum half-life study; ND2:SmoA1 autochthonous medulloblastoma mice on a C57BL/6 background (hemizygous or homozygous, symptomatic) for the imaging study; sex not reported
in_vivo_species.quote: Two month old wild-type C57BL/6 mice (Charles River) were intravenously injected with 50 μL of 40 μM cyclized CTX:Cy5.5 through the tail vein.

ex_vivo_detail: Serum stability assay in 100% human male serum (Sigma) at 37 C with 20 µM peptide, sampled in triplicate at 0, 1, 3, 6, 10, 16 and 24 h and quantified by RP-HPLC; PBS-incubated peptide served as control. Ex vivo biophotonic imaging of brains harvested from dosed mice was also performed, but that tissue came from animals dosed in vivo.

agents.name: cyclic chlorotoxin:Cy5.5 (cyclized CTX:Cy5.5)
agents.sequence_source: Fig. 1B is said to show 'The amino acid sequences of linear, Ala and Arg substituted and cyclic chlorotoxin', but no one-letter sequence is printed in the body text; the body states only that the cyclizing linker is GAGAAGG and that CTX is a 36 amino acid peptide with Lys at positions 15, 23 and 27
agents.chemical_identifier: backbone-cyclized chlorotoxin joined N- to C-terminus by a GAGAAGG linker via intramolecular native chemical ligation; conjugated to Cy5.5-NHS ester (Invitrogen)
agents.group_n: n = 3 per time point (serum half-life); n = 5 (functional imaging)
agents.group_n_quote: Blood was collected for three animals at each time point.
agents.dose: 50 µL of 40 µM bioconjugate per mouse
agents.dose_route_quote: Two month old wild-type C57BL/6 mice (Charles River) were intravenously injected with 50 μL of 40 μM cyclized CTX:Cy5.5 through the tail vein.
agents.half_life_matrix: mouse serum/plasma after a single intravenous injection
agents.pk_quote: Cyclized CTX:Cy5.5 had a serum half-life of 11 h, showing that cyclization does not extend the in vivo serum half-life when compared with linear CTX:Cy5.5
agents.pk_section: RESULTS (Serum half-life of cyclized and linear CTX:Cy5.5 bioconjugates)

concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Blood was collected 1, 3, 6, 10, 24, and 49 h after injection of cyclic CTX:Cy5.5 and fluorescent intensity in the serum was measured using the Odyssey Imaging System.
concentration_time_figure.note: Fig. 3B plots serum fluorescent intensity (concentration proxy, read against a standard curve) versus time after a single i.v. injection of cyclic CTX:Cy5.5, n = 3. Fig. 3A is an ex vivo human-serum stability curve plotting percent intact peptide versus incubation time (0-24 h).

bioanalytical_method: Fluorescence of the Cy5.5 label in plasma read on an Odyssey Imaging System (Li-Cor) 700 nm channel against a standard curve of cyclized CTX:Cy5.5 in wild-type C57BL/6 plasma; RP-HPLC integration at 215 nm for the human-serum stability assay
bioanalytical_quote: The plates were scanned on the Odyssey Imaging System (Li-Cor Bioscience) using the 700 nm channel.
notes: Only cyclic CTX:Cy5.5 was pharmacokinetically profiled in this study (11 h, no error term). The ~14 h half-life for linear CTX:Cy5.5 is stated in the body as prior knowledge ('We knew, in advance of the current studies') rather than as data generated here, and no dose, group size or error term is given for it. No Cmax, tmax, AUC or clearance is reported for any agent. Doses are given as volume x molarity (50 uL of 40 uM) with no mg/kg equivalent. No amino-acid sequences appear in the body text; Fig. 1B is stated to contain them but the figure image is not available in this text file. The half-life measures the Cy5.5 fluorescent signal, not intact peptide.
